description: CAPABILITY CLASS -> REASONING EFFORT. The third dimension, beside CLASS -> MODEL (routing/capabilities.json) and MODEL FAMILY -> SHIM (routing/shims.json), and kept here for the same reason they are kept apart: one file, one decision. How much thinking a class gets is a property of the WORK, so it is one vocabulary here and not a column per provider; how a provider SPELLS it is that provider's adapter (tools/fabric/routing.py), and whether a given model admits a level is the adapter's per-model table. Effort exists as a routed value because it was not one: every model the fabric had pinned happened to default to `high`, and Opus 5.5 was the first that did not — moving code-high to it would have dropped every session a level with no commit and nothing to review (docs/live-checks/2026-09-23-opus-5-5.md). A model's own default is never the fabric's decision.
levels_note: Ordered, least to most. The union of the vendors' scales, not any one vendor's: Anthropic admits low..max, OpenAI all seven, xAI none..xhigh, DeepSeek low/high/max, GLM-5.3-Flash low/high/max. A level is an ORDINAL, never a magnitude — no vendor asserts that its `high` means another's, and neither does this file. What a class asks for is clamped DOWN to the nearest level its model admits, by the fabric, before the request leaves: the vendors disagree on the failure mode (OpenAI returns 400, xAI and Claude Code clamp silently, GLM-5.3-Flash errors, DeepSeek remaps), and a routing decision must not mean two different things depending on who serves it.
session_note: A level, or a capability class whose level to take — as routing/profiles.json's own `session` may name a class. Naming the class keeps the session's thinking with the session's model: both are code-high on the anthropic path, and one edit moves both. A layer that gives one agent's session another model does not move its level: architect-cto-01's session is Fable 5.1 (routing/profiles.json) and still thinks at code-high's level, not code-plan's.

notes.code-low: null, not a level: the harness's own model registry gives claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 the capability list ["context_management"] — no "effort" — and a model without it is gated out before a request is built, so no level is ever sent. So code-low's `low` is not a downgrade here, it is nothing at all, and the class runs on whatever the model does by itself. Acknowledged rather than silently dropped. If code-low ever moves to a model that takes effort, delete this line and check() will start judging it again.
notes.code-medium: No override: code-medium asks `medium` and claude-sonnet-5 admits it. Recorded because the model's OWN default is `high` (registry, 2.1.280), so the fabric is deliberately asking for less than the vendor would give. That is the routing decision working as intended — a level chosen here rather than inherited — but it is a real reduction and should be seen as one.

notes.code-plan: code-plan asks for xhigh; deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro distinguishes low/high/max and documents xhigh -> high, so `high` is what it would serve. Written down because the alternative is a level of thinking lost between the routing file and the wire. Note the consequence while this column stands: code-high, code-plan and code-review all resolve to the same model AND now the same effort, so on the broker those three classes differ in neither. That is a true statement about today's broker column, not a property of the design — on the anthropic path they are high/xhigh/xhigh.
notes.code-review: The owner's decision of 2026-09-23: the review class thinks at xhigh, one level above code-high, because a review is judgement work of the same kind as code-plan and its failure mode — a defect that merges — is the expensive one. On the broker the reviewer is deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro, which distinguishes low/high/max and documents xhigh -> high, so `high` is what it would serve; written down rather than lost. On plain claude the reviewer is claude-opus-5[1m], which admits xhigh (the harness strips [1m] before its capability lookup), and gets it.
